messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: non-comformable argument - geom_sf
parts:
Hi there,

I've been using geom_sf for a little while now. I am truly impressed with its tight integration into ggplot2 and although I know it is still in development, I am very excited about it as a part of ggplot2.

That said, I am experiencing some issues that I haven't been able to figure out. I've attached some shapefiles to this email. I can't figure out why these won't output a figure with geom_sf(). 

library(sf)
devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)

##To read the data in:
lakes_out <- st_read("lakes.shp") 

## Now this works fine:
plot(lakes_out$geometry)

## But if I try to use geom_sf() like this:
ggplot(lakes_out) +
  geom_sf()

## I get this error:
Error in x %*% Mat : non-conformable arguments

I've been having trouble making a reproducible example with this because every shapefile that I find online (e.g.: http://www.geog.uoregon.edu/GeogR/examples/maps_examples01.htm) behave as they should. So I apologize for having to include attachments here but this is the only way I could think to do this.

Ultimately I am trying to figure out why these shapefile components can't plot with geom_sf when they are fine with plot(). But more generally I am wondering if anyone can suggest a diagnostic tool to compare two objects read in with read_sf to predict when this is going to happen?

Thanks in advance,

Sam

messages.subject: RE: non-comformable argument - geom_sf
parts:
I got your geom_sf code to work with your shapefile by removing the Z dimension. I did this in ArcGIS (http://support.esri.com/technical-article/000010389) because I don’t have a lot of skills manipulating spatial data in R.

 

HTH

 

Seth

messages.author: ddc91303cb21ac62
messages.subject: Re: non-comformable argument - geom_sf
parts: Ah yes an excellent sleuth job here. Turns out that the wonderful folks developing "sf" have anticipated this issue and the function st_zm complete solved my issues. Full solution:

library(sf)
devtools::install_github("tidyverse/ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)

##To read the data in:
lakes_out <- st_read("lakes.shp")

lakes_out <- st_zm(lakes_out)

ggplot(lakes_out) +
  geom_sf()

Works!

Thanks Seth.
